solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Report murder? (8)

blocks.note: a noun here: the kind of report a war correspondent sends home
a verb here: a polite, old-fashioned word for killing off

annotation.surface: A newspaper promises a report on a murder.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the two words are not a headline pair but two separate meanings of one word.
annotation.definitionFit: A war correspondent files a dispatch, and a hitman dispatches his target.

entries.clue: Prove false, young lady excoriated attractive men (6)

indicatorNotes.excoriated: to excoriate is to strip the skin, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society lady
HUNKS with its first and last letters stripped

annotation.surface: A young woman tears into some good-looking men, proving their claims false.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Excoriated' reads as harsh criticism, but here it means literally skinned.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: exposing a myth or a quack remedy as hollow is debunking it.

entries.clue: Passionate tale entertains medium (6)

indicatorNotes.entertains: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so STORY holds M

blocks.note: a tale is a story
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

annotation.surface: A romantic story holds a spiritualist medium's attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic at a seance; it is just the size label M.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative weather: a love affair full of fierce rows and reconciliations is called stormy.

entries.clue: Gold polish turned base of crown reddish-brown (6)

indicatorNotes.turned: turned round, so RUB is written backwards
indicatorNotes.base of: in a down clue the base of a word is its bottom, that is, last letter

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to polish something is to rub it
last letter of CROWN

annotation.surface: A gold crown, polished and turned over, shows a reddish-brown base.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crown' tempts you toward royalty or hair; only its final letter is wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: Auburn is a reddish-brown shade, usually of hair.

entries.clue: Companion taking tea, say, in opening of novel (7,3)

indicatorNotes.taking: the companion takes the T inside
indicatorNotes.say: T is how 'tea' is said, so 'tea, say' gives the letter T

blocks.note: a chaperone accompanies a young person
the letter T is pronounced like 'tea'

annotation.surface: A companion takes tea at the start of a novel, like a scene from Austen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Companion' looks like the definition, but it is only the outer word; the answer is the opening of the novel.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: books are divided into numbered sections, and the first of them is where the story begins.

entries.clue: Bad knight caught in incursion (6)

indicatorNotes.in: in its plain sense of placement: the knight and the catch end up inside the raid

blocks.note: a raid is an incursion into enemy ground
N is the chess notation for knight
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

annotation.surface: A villainous knight is captured during a raid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad knight' reads as a villain, but 'Bad' stands alone as the definition, as in butter gone off.
annotation.definitionFit: Bad in the sense of spoiled: butter or oil that has gone off smells rancid.

entries.clue: Sailor finally falls in the drink (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the final letter of FALLS

blocks.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
last letter of FALLS
taken as written

annotation.surface: A sailor at last falls overboard into the sea.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The drink' is slang for the sea, which is where the surface puts the sailor; the definition is just 'drink'.
annotation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong aniseed-flavoured spirit.

entries.clue: Material boys discovered chasing dog across ring road (8)

indicatorNotes.discovered: uncovered, so BOYS loses its outer letters
indicatorNotes.chasing: a chaser runs behind its quarry, so the boys' letters come after the dog-and-road part
indicatorNotes.across: CUR spreads across O and RD

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a ring is shaped like O
standard abbreviation
BOYS with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: Boys chase a dog across a ring road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ring road' reads as one thing, a road round a town; it splits into O and RD.
annotation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ribbed cotton fabric.

entries.clue: Flatten misshapen shield employing standard method (8)

indicatorNotes.misshapen: bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.employing: SHIELD uses MO alongside it in the mix

blocks.note: taken as written
MO, modus operandi, is a standard way of working

annotation.surface: Someone batters a warped shield flat using the usual technique.
annotation.walkthrough: MO stands for modus operandi, Latin for method of operating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the building site: knocking a structure to the ground.

entries.clue: Spoilt child clutches medal broken by Welsh bully (8)

indicatorNotes.broken by: W splits OBE into O and BE

blocks.note: a brat is a spoilt child
the OBE is a British honour, Order of the British Empire
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A spoilt child grabs a medal off a Welsh bully.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Welsh bully' looks like a person, but 'Welsh' is only W and 'bully' is the verb definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: intimidating someone with stern looks and harsh words.

entries.clue: Retreat from wood pursued by horned beast (6)

indicatorNotes.pursued by: ASH comes first with RAM behind it

blocks.note: ash is a type of wood
a ram is a horned male sheep

annotation.surface: Someone flees a forest with a horned animal on their heels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retreat' reads as a verb, running away; it is the noun, a place of spiritual withdrawal.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a Hindu hermitage where people withdraw for meditation is one kind of retreat.

entries.clue: Maureen struggling to admit model’s skilled in arithmetic (8)

indicatorNotes.to admit: the rearranged letters let T inside

blocks.note: taken as written
the Model T was Ford's famous car

annotation.surface: Maureen reluctantly admits that a model is good at sums.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A numerate person is competent with numbers.

entries.clue: Publication damning US ally is oddly ignored (6)

indicatorNotes.oddly ignored: the odd-numbered letters are dropped, keeping the even ones

blocks.note: letters 2, 4, 6... of DAMNINGUSALLY

annotation.surface: A newspaper condemning America's ally is disregarded.
annotation.walkthrough: The political surface hides a simple letter pick.
annotation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, such as a children's comic annual.

entries.clue: Blend ultimately potent drink after three months without whiskey (10)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the last letter of POTENT
indicatorNotes.after: the T and WINE come after INTER

blocks.note: WINTER lasts three months; remove W, which is whiskey in the NATO alphabet
last letter of POTENT
wine is a drink

annotation.surface: Mixing a strong drink after three dry months off the whisky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Three months' asks you to think of a season rather than month names.
annotation.definitionFit: To intertwine things is to twist them together, blending them.

entries.clue: Formal meals initially cancelled by heads of top-flight rugby clubs (10)

indicatorNotes.initially cancelled: the first letter is struck out
indicatorNotes.heads of: the head is the top or front of something, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of TOP and RUGBY
LUNCHEONS without its first letter

annotation.surface: Rugby club dinners are called off by the top-flight bosses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rugby clubs' reads as a unit; 'clubs' is the definition, meaning the heavy sticks.
annotation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short club carried by police.

entries.clue: Bid to control outcome for criminal (8)

blocks.note: a bid is an offer
the end is the outcome

annotation.surface: An attempt to fix the result of a trial for a crook.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bid to control outcome' reads as match-fixing; 'to control' means to hold within.
annotation.definitionFit: An offender is someone who has committed a crime.

entries.clue: One might say waiter’s high on Ecstasy (2,2,4)

indicatorNotes.high: intoxicated, so WAITERS's letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue WAITERS sits on top of E

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

annotation.surface: Someone remarks that the waiter seems to be on drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High' is the drug-trip sense as the anagram signal, and the apostrophe is just part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: As it were is a hedge meaning 'so to speak' or 'one might say'.

entries.clue: Steerpike’s peevishness about church upset halfwit (8)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns CE upside down to EC

blocks.note: Steerpike is the setter, so the setter's = I'm
bile is bad temper
CE is the Church of England

annotation.surface: The setter's irritation at the church has upset a fool.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters often use their pen-name for 'I' or 'me'; here 'Steerpike's' is I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are dated insults for someone foolish.

entries.clue: Trained frogmen guarding island silence shopkeeper (10)

indicatorNotes.Trained: the frogmen's letters are drilled into a new order
indicatorNotes.guarding: they hold I and SH between them

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
sh! is a call for silence

annotation.surface: Trained divers protect an island and keep a shopkeeper quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: The frogmen belong to the world of the answer, fish, which helps hide the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A fishmonger keeps a shop selling fish.

entries.clue: Animal droppings mostly dumped in middle of Adriatic (6)

indicatorNotes.middle of: take the central letters of ADRIATIC

blocks.note: the two central letters of ADRIATIC
GUANO, seabird droppings, without the final O

annotation.surface: Animal waste has been dumped in the middle of the Adriatic Sea.
annotation.walkthrough: Guano is the droppings of seabirds or bats, collected as fertiliser.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a large tropical lizard is one example of an animal.

entries.clue: Partaking in fracas in opulent entertainment venue (6)

indicatorNotes.Partaking in: the answer takes part of the following words

blocks.note: fraCAS IN Opulent

annotation.surface: Someone joins in a brawl at a lavish nightspot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Opulent' reads as describing the venue, but it only lends its O to the hidden letters; a fracas is a noisy brawl.
annotation.definitionFit: A casino is a plush venue for gambling and shows.

entries.clue: Promotional footage regularly claimed Greens made it up (6)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means written bottom to top

blocks.note: even letters of GREENSMADEIT

annotation.surface: Campaign video says the Green Party invented something.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made it up' reads as fabricating, but 'up' is the reversal in a down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A teaser is a short trailer released to build interest.

entries.clue: Revolutionary bumps into European count (6)

indicatorNotes.Revolutionary: turning round, so MEETSE is read backwards

blocks.note: to bump into someone is to meet them
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A revolutionary runs into a European aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman; it is the verb, as in 'I count it an honour'.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to regard as, as in 'I would count it an honour'.

entries.clue: Remain at a standstill in Spooner’s horse country (8)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: Dr Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: a nag is an old horse; it gives up its N and takes ST
a state is a country; it hands over ST and takes the N

annotation.surface: Standing still in horse country.
annotation.walkthrough: Say 'nag state' and swap the opening sounds of the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stop moving or developing.

entries.clue: Retracted affidavit, essentially about wife meeting Italian on vacation (4,2)

indicatorNotes.essentially: take the essence, the central letter
indicatorNotes.on vacation: vacated, so emptied of its inside letters

blocks.note: the middle letter of AFFIDAVIT
re means about, concerning
standard abbreviation
ITALIAN emptied to its outer letters

annotation.surface: A sworn statement about a wife's holiday with an Italian was withdrawn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retracted affidavit' reads as one legal phrase; the first word alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To draw in claws is to retract them, so retracted means drew in.

entries.clue: Salient changes involving international lists (8)

indicatorNotes.involving: the rearranged letters take I in

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: Key amendments to an international list.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Salient' looks like an adjective describing the changes; it is only the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A litany is a long tedious list, as in a litany of complaints.

entries.clue: Taking portion of meagre fee, realtor flipped joint (6)

indicatorNotes.Taking portion of: the answer is a portion of the words that follow

blocks.note: meagRE FEE Realtor

annotation.surface: An estate agent, grabbing a cut of a small fee, loses their temper over a property.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipped' suggests losing one's temper, and 'joint' a property; realtor is the US word for an estate agent.
annotation.definitionFit: Drug slang: both words name a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

entries.clue: Keep going on about extremely baroque party (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of BAROQUE
Labour is a British political party

annotation.surface: Someone drones on about an extremely ornate party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a celebration, which 'baroque' supports; it is the British Labour Party.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: labouring a point in an argument means dwelling on it tediously.
